note: Hilly upland forest above the Mississippi south of Hannibal, holding the highest point in Ralls County; the river frontage has little access. Camping is at a gravel lot in the woods on a short drive off Highway 79 at the area's south edge. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Designated Camping Sites'; brochure 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots', 14 days in 30; map legend has Primitive Camping; GIS camp 200 at gravel lot 895 off Highway 79. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin fine. Not waterfront kept. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'. Brochure: 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots. No unattended open campfires allowed. Stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. Groups of more than 10 campers require a special use permit.' The map (9/4/2019) legend lists Primitive Camping (the symbol did not render legibly in the PDF - poppler reported PostScript errors), and MDC's GIS has camping point 200 at gravel lot 895, 6 m apart: a mapped designated spot at a gravel lot, not a boat-ramp lot. Imagery: a ~40 x 30 m gravel lot in woods ~45 m north of Highway 79 on a short gravel drive. A 23-ft rig fits. No ford/4WD/rig wording.

WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): area page 'Although the area is bordered by 2.3 miles of Mississippi River, access to the river is limited.' The lot is ~2 km from the river behind wooded hills and the railroad.
PHONE: area page and brochure '(573) 248-2530' match.
